title: Driver Monitoring System
blurb: Real-time driver monitoring on a Raspberry Pi. Split into two processes over ZeroMQ so camera capture never blocks on inference latency. Detects phone use and eye closure, locks onto a single tracked driver, and scores risk from gaze duration, phone presence, and PERCLOS. I dropped the torch runtime in favor of raw ncnn to save roughly 150MB and eliminate a crash class specific to the Pi 4B.

title: cura
blurb: A robotic feeding assistant for hospital patients. Drives a Piper arm over CAN to deliver a water bottle, coordinated by a FastAPI state machine with a hard emergency stop. The arm's SDK assumes Linux, so I built the macOS CAN path from scratch with gs_usb and SLCAN, then found and fixed a reconnect failure and a segfault in it. Also built the vision to arm bridge.

title: Accordion
blurb: Context window management for AI coding agents: fold, unfold, and pin any part of an agent's context without ever deleting it. I built a WebSocket based conductor, an alternative automatic folding strategy, then returned later to ship the system prompt as a first class, non foldable dial: capture hook, token accounting, wire protocol bump, new UI panel, 746 tests passing. Also built the Windows release installer workflow.

title: SIGNAL
blurb: Human in the loop dispatch software for wildfire surge events. Four agents triage calls, route the nearest unit, and voice a briefing, under a strict rule that AI never speaks to a caller directly. I built the entire real-time dashboard: auto-reconnecting WebSocket state over eight message types, a Leaflet map with live fire perimeter, override and hold gates, plus live call transcription and a phone-in voice agent.
